extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, and newsroom staff (readers interested in editorial standards)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for issuing corrections, clarifications, and updates to news and blog posts; emphasizes accuracy, attribution, labeling, and transparency when fixing factual or interpretive errors. Useful for newsroom editors and writers who must decide when and how to correct published content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct factual errors promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: When published content contains incorrect facts (names, job titles, dates, numbers, locations, spellings, bylines, headlines, illustrations), issue a correction that states what was wrong and what the correct information is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the log: corrected misspelled names (e.g., Jane Boulen), misstated job titles (e.g., Marissa Mayer), wrong numbers (e.g., markets covered by Yahoo! Local News), misidentified locations (e.g., Union Univ. is in Jackson, Tenn.), incorrect bylines, and wrong headlines. Corrections should be explicit about the specific error and the fix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label changes clearly as 'CORRECTION', 'CLARIFICATION', or 'UPDATE'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use explicit labels (CORRECTION, CLARIFICATION, UPDATE, UPDATE / CLARIFICATION) to indicate the nature of the post-publication change so readers know whether a factual error, an imprecision, or a content update occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page consistently prefixes items with CORRECTION, CLARIFICATION, UPDATE / CLARIFICATION, etc. Place the label prominently (often at or near the top) and explain the change in a concise note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain the context and cause of the error when useful
rubrics_metrics.description: When relevant, describe how the error arose (e.g., misreading a source, relying on an incorrect third-party story) to provide transparency about the mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: noting that an earlier version 'did not reflect PolitiFact’s updated ratings' or that an item 'was based on a Reuters item that turned out to be inaccurate.' Such explanations help readers understand whether the error was internal or inherited from another source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish 'clarification' from 'correction' for imprecise or ambiguous wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'clarification' when the original wording could mislead or be interpreted imprecisely but may not be strictly false; use 'correction' for verifiably incorrect facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: clarifying the circumstances under which a site disables comments vs. correcting a misspelled name. Label choice signals severity/quality of the error to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute subjective assessments and opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments of editorial quality and other subjective judgments should be attributed to identifiable sources rather than presented as the publication's unquestioned fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording: 'Assessments of editorial quality involve personal, subjective judgments and should be attributed accordingly.' Also: 'Inclusion of that assertion without clear attribution violated Poynter’s publishing guidelines.' When making evaluative statements, include who said it or base it on attributed reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be precise about technical and legal distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid imprecise or legally significant language (e.g., murder vs. manslaughter, unemployment rate vs. raw counts); correct and clarify when a story misstates such distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: corrected 'Murder is a legal term...' note to reflect possible manslaughter or self-defense distinctions; clarified difference between number of people without jobs and the unemployment rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct or remove erroneous illustrations and multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: If images, graphics, or multimedia elements are incorrect or misleading, remove or replace them and note the change in a correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: removed an incorrect illustration that misidentified a painting; corrected which television station aired a documentary and adjusted dates for video projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix misattributions and misquotations
rubrics_metrics.description: When quotes, attributions, or reported statements are misattributed (wrong speaker, wrong source), correct the attribution and explain the error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include correcting a misattribution of a phrase to the Declaration of Independence and fixing who turned whose argument in a discussion. State the corrected attribution and, when relevant, how it was mistaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct erroneous external references and links
rubrics_metrics.description: If the story contains incorrect URLs, wrong references to organizations/projects, or misidentified external resources, update the item and correct the link or reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: fixing a wrong URL for TenByTen.org; correcting identification of Congresspedia vs OpenCongress; updating that a correction is at a different URL from the original story and linking to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publishing proprietary or sensitive information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish proprietary, confidential, or proprietary-dollar amounts that should not be released; remove or redact such details if mistakenly published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: removed a dollar amount for an ad deal because it was proprietary information that should not have been released publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid facilitating deals or transactional guidance in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: If reporting includes contact information or transactional detail that could unintentionally facilitate deals or business actions, edit the story to report without facilitating such transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: edited an item that had included contact information and deadlines for possible deals to avoid appearing to facilitate deal-making; report what is happening without providing facilitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update stories when new information becomes available and note the change
rubrics_metrics.description: When subsequent facts, corrections, or publisher updates surface (including third-party corrections), update the story and add an explanatory note or link to the new information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: adding an update that a site later posted a correction at a different URL; noting when PolitiFact updated ratings and adjusting the story accordingly. Put update/clarification at top and link to supporting materials when possible.
